summary: Confirmed DONE, all landed in 60633eff3 (#710), with 79b492cd6 and 8fb94df00 on top. Server: each live orchestration event is measured once. orchestrationEventBytes memoizes the size per event object in a WeakMap. The engine's PubSub hands the same object to every subscriber, so the offer, the coalescer (push, supersede, emit), the batch release and the chunk splitter of every subscription share one measurement, and the byte ledger stays balanced by construction. Release and recordLiveDequeued run once per drained array, and replay metrics once per replay page. Replay metrics: every record() is O(1) via incremental sums and RunningMax. Gauges are written only when the aggregate value changes. A stale maximum settles synchronously for up to 8 subscriptions, otherwise through one delayed rescan per stream per second. I traced RunningMax update/add/remove/settle and found no correctness bug. Client: supervision.ts has no JSON.stringify or TextEncoder left. Live events size only the changed row (text.length for messages, an O(nodes) walk for activities and plans). Snapshots and pages use the same walk, which treats string length as O(1). Eviction planning and the per-environment timer reconcile are coalesced to once per delivered chunk (microtask), and on web the reconcile runs once per animation-frame batch. Remaining per-event costs are constant per event or per subscription, not O(S) per event or O(text) per subscription.

evidence.note: WeakMap<OrchestrationEvent, number> cache. approximateJsonBytes runs at most once per event object.
PubSub.publish passes the same persisted event object to every subscriber (subscribeDomainEvents at :679-680), so the cache is shared across subscriptions.
All coalescer measurements go through orchestrationEventBytes and hit the cache. The offer receives the precomputed size.
offerOrchestrationLiveEventOrFail uses input.eventBytes. It measures only when no precomputed size is passed and a ledger exists.
releaseQueuedEventsBytes sums cached sizes for a drained batch and does one Ref.update.
drainLiveQueue releases bytes and calls recordLiveDequeued once per drained array.
Replay metrics are recorded per replay page via tapArray. The chunk splitter's sizeOf uses the cached size.
RunningMax keeps the maximum in O(1) with a holder count and a stale flag. I traced the update, add and remove branches and they are correct.
StreamReplayAggregate keeps the buffer-depth sum and maxima incrementally. It rescans only stale maxima.
publishAggregateFor writes only the gauges whose aggregate changed, and returns Effect.void otherwise.
record() is O(1). It settles synchronously only for up to 8 subscriptions, otherwise once per WS_REPLAY_METRICS_SETTLE_MS (1 s) per stream.
The walk estimate counts strings as length+2 (O(1) per string), so its cost is O(nodes), not O(text bytes).
retainedRowWrite sizes only the changed row: text.length for message-sent, the walk for an activity or plan. Other events are not measured.
Per-row ledger. The total is updated incrementally. Snapshot and page walks run once per snapshot or page.
applyEvent schedules eviction, which runs once per delivered chunk (afterCurrentChunk microtask at :40-42).
The public reconcileThreadDetailSubscriptionEvictionForEnvironment is the deduped scheduler, so timer re-arming runs once per chunk per environment.
Web calls reconcile once per frame-batched thread-detail commit (createEnvironmentEventBatcher plus scheduleStreamBatchFrame).
Mobile calls reconcile per event, but it goes through the same microtask-deduped scheduler.

fixDefects: No defect in the implemented fix. Minor residuals that do not reopen the finding: (1) The first measurement of each live event is still a full JSON.stringify plus TextEncoder.encode (packages/shared/src/perf.ts:54-66, called from orchestrationStreamBatching.ts:29). I measured about 14 us for a 20 KB streaming subagent activity and about 68 us for 100 KB, once per event, including frames the coalescer later drops. A walk would be about 0.4 us. Keeping exact UTF-8 bytes is defensible, though: they feed the 256 KiB chunk splitter and the 4 MiB queue budget, and a length walk undercounts non-ASCII by up to 3x and escaped control characters by up to 6x. (2) updateGauge (wsReplayMetrics.ts:252-256) builds a new Metric.withAttributes transform on every write. In effect@4.0.2 that creates a fresh merged attribute set, so the base gauge's hook recomputes makeKey (Object.entries, sort, JSON.stringify) on each write. liveBufferDepth and replayLag change on almost every enqueue and dequeue, so this is about 2-3 small key builds per event per subscription: constant, microseconds each. (3) An adjacent path outside this finding has the same pattern: the terminal subscriber ledger measures each terminal event twice per subscriber with approximateJsonBytes, at offer (apps/server/src/ws/terminalRpc.ts:100) and again at release (:73). Terminal events are shared objects from Manager.publishEvent (apps/server/src/terminal/Layers/Manager.ts:1056-1067).
implementationSketch: Optional low-value follow-ups only. (a) Terminal ledger: in apps/server/src/ws/terminalRpc.ts, add a module-level WeakMap<TerminalEvent, number> helper, terminalEventBytes, mirroring orchestrationEventBytes. Use it in makeTerminalSubscriberOffer (:100) and releaseTerminalSubscriberEvent (:73), so each output chunk is measured once across all subscribers and the offer and release values match exactly. Extend the existing terminalRpc tests: a ledger returns to 0 after offering and releasing the same events, and the byte-budget resync still trips. (b) Replay gauges: in apps/server/src/wsReplayMetrics.ts, memoize the attributed gauges per stream kind, e.g. a Record<WsReplayStreamKind, {replayDepth, replayLag, liveBufferDepth, liveBufferHighWater}> built once with Metric.withAttributes. updateGauge then reuses one transform and its merged attribute object, so the base hook's key cache hits. Covered by the existing wsReplayMetrics.test.ts aggregate tests. (c) Only if profiling shows it matters: compute the server size with Buffer.byteLength(JSON.stringify(event), 'utf8') in a server-local helper to skip the Uint8Array copy (about 15-20% cheaper). Do not switch to a length walk unless the chunk and queue budgets get a safety factor for multi-byte and escaped content.
decisionReason: Server-local CPU micro-optimizations. They change no protocol, auth, E2EE, hosted lifecycle or product behaviour.
